 ## Output and readiness
 
-Events are thin: `type` says what changed and `data.api_url` points at the changed object, such as the review or the pull request. Consumers fetch it when they need details.
+Events are thin: `type` says what changed and `data.api_url` points at the changed object, such as the review, the pull request, or the check suite. Consumers fetch it when they need details. Check suite events also carry `data.conclusion`; a pull request usually has several check suites, each sending its own event, so consumers waiting for all checks read them after each event.
 
 `--jq` and `--template` format each event separately, like `gh api`. They are mutually exclusive and validated before subscribing. jq results are printed one per line, with strings unquoted. An expression or template that fails on an event ends the command rather than reconnecting. Output is JSON whether or not stdout is a terminal.
 
@@ -41,6 +41,8 @@ Preview requests use the configured HTTP client. Only github.com is supported; G
 
 When `internal/agents` detects an agent caller, a successful `gh pr create` of a github.com pull request, a successful non-browser `gh pr view` of a github.com pull request that is not merged or closed, and a successful `gh api` GET of a github.com `repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/NUMBER` endpoint or any of its subpaths, given as a path or as an absolute `https://api.github.com` URL, print a hint on stderr for waiting on its events instead of polling, addressed to agents that need to wait for the pull request to be reviewed, merged, or closed before continuing. The hint puts a copyable `gh event listen` command on its own line, with full event type names. It notes that the command prints the first event as a JSON line and exits, and that it can be run again to wait for the next one. It deliberately does not mention `--follow`: agents offered it chose it even for one-off waits, ran it in the background, and were never resumed. It suggests `--timeout` with an example. It also notes that events carry no details, that changes made before the listener starts are missed so the pull request should be read once it is running, and points to `gh event listen --help` for other event types. `gh api` does not know the pull request state, so its hint is also shown for merged or closed pull requests. Human invocations, other hosts, stdout, JSON output, and exit status are unchanged. The `gh pr` and `gh pr view` help texts also point to `gh event listen` for github.com, and, like the `gh event` help, state that changes made before the listener starts are not reported.
 
+For an agent caller, `gh run watch` and `gh run view` of a workflow run that is not completed and belongs to a github.com pull request print a similar hint on stderr, addressed to agents that need to wait for the checks of the pull request to finish. It suggests listening to `com.github.pull_request.check_suite.status.changed.v1` for the pull request, with the same notes, except that it explains that each check suite sends its own event with its conclusion, and that the checks should be read with `gh pr checks` after each event, running the listener again while any are pending. `gh run watch` prints it before it starts watching, so it is seen even if the watch is stopped. `gh run view` prints it with `--json` too, but not with `--web` or `--log`. The `gh run watch` and `gh run view` help texts point to `gh event listen` for waiting on the workflow runs of a github.com pull request.
+
 ## Eval use
 
 The shipped `gh` skill at `skills/gh` documents `gh event listen`. Evaluate it from the working tree, or compare it with the version on trunk, which has no event guidance until this change merges:

 func PrintListenHint(w io.Writer, pullRequestURL string) {
+	printListenHint(w, pullRequestURL, listenHint{
+		purpose:  "if you need to wait for this pull request to be reviewed, merged, or closed before continuing",
+		events:   "com.github.pull_request.review.submitted.v1,com.github.pull_request.state.changed.v1",
+		readNote: "Events carry no details; read the pull request to see what changed.",
+		snapshot: "the pull request",
+	})
+}
+
+// PrintChecksListenHint suggests `gh event listen` for the check suites of the given pull request URL, because agents
+// tend to poll workflow runs when asked to wait for a pull request's checks to finish. It prints nothing for hosts the
+// Events API does not support.
+func PrintChecksListenHint(w io.Writer, pullRequestURL string) {
+	printListenHint(w, pullRequestURL, listenHint{
+		purpose: "if you need to wait for the checks of this pull request to finish before continuing",
+		events:  "com.github.pull_request.check_suite.status.changed.v1",
+		readNote: fmt.Sprintf("Each check suite, such as a workflow run, sends its own event with its conclusion "+
+			"when it completes; after each event, read the checks with `gh pr checks %s`, and if any are still "+
+			"pending, run the listener again.", pullRequestURL),
+		snapshot: "the checks",
+	})
+}
+
+type listenHint struct {
+	// purpose completes "hint: ..." and says what the agent may be waiting for.
+	purpose string
+	// events is the comma-separated event types to listen to.
+	events string
+	// readNote says what an event carries and what to read after it.
+	readNote string
+	// snapshot names what to read once the listener is running.
+	snapshot string
+}
+
+func printListenHint(w io.Writer, pullRequestURL string, h listenHint) {
 	u, err := url.Parse(pullRequestURL)
 	if pullRequestURL == "" || err != nil || !client.SupportedHost(u.Hostname()) {

-		    gh event listen --resource %[2]s --event com.github.pull_request.review.submitted.v1,com.github.pull_request.state.changed.v1
+		hint: %[2]s, use this instead of polling:
+		    gh event listen --resource %[3]s --event %[4]s
 		  - It prints the first event as a JSON line on stdout and exits; run it again to wait for the next one.
 		  - Add %[1]s--timeout%[1]s to stop waiting after a while, for example %[1]s--timeout 30m%[1]s; it then exits with status 8.
-		  - Events carry no details; read the pull request to see what changed.
-		  - It misses changes made before it starts, so read the pull request once it is running.
+		  - %[5]s
+		  - It misses changes made before it starts, so read %[6]s once it is running.
 		  - See %[1]sgh event listen --help%[1]s for other event types.
 		  - Event subscriptions are in preview and may not be enabled for your account.
-	`, "`", pullRequestURL))
+	`, "`", h.purpose, pullRequestURL, h.events, h.readNote, h.snapshot))

+}

-`--resource` takes the pull request URL. `--event` takes full event type names, separated by commas or by repeating the flag: `com.github.pull_request.review.submitted.v1` (a review was submitted), `com.github.pull_request.state.changed.v1` (merged, closed, reopened, marked ready for review, or converted to draft), `com.github.pull_request.head.changed.v1` (the head branch changed), and `com.github.pull_request.merge_conflict.v1` (a merge conflict appeared). By default the command exits after the first event; `--count N` exits after N events, and `--follow` keeps listening until stopped. For a one-off wait, such as a single review, merge, or close, use the default, and once the event arrives and you have read the result, finish the task instead of waiting for more. Read it once after each event to learn what changed, for example `gh api URL` or `gh pr view NUMBER --json reviews,state,mergedAt`. A comment or requested change is not an approval, and a pull request closed without merging is not permission to pull. If you were waiting for a merge and the pull request closes without merging, stop and tell the user rather than waiting for it to be reopened. Initial inspection and event-triggered reads are not polling.
+
+To wait for CI, listen for `com.github.pull_request.check_suite.status.changed.v1`. A pull request usually has several check suites, and each sends its own event when it completes, with `data.conclusion` such as `success` or `failure`. One event does not mean all checks are done: after each event, read the checks once with `gh pr checks NUMBER`, and stop when none are pending. Use `--follow`, or run the one-shot listener again, to wait for the remaining suites.
 
 The API is live-only: events that happened before the stream attached are never delivered. Start the listener as a separate first tool call, before inspecting the PR. Do not launch the stream and initial snapshot in the same parallel batch. Wait until stderr reports that the listener is listening for events, then take the initial snapshot. A generic "background command started" message is not enough. This ordering closes the gap between reading the state and listening for changes.
